source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Know When They're Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification
finding: A probe on hidden states at intermediate-answer positions predicts whether that answer is correct. It works as a machine feeling of rightness. Models hold this signal but do not use it to stop.
numbers: DeepSeek-R1-Distill 1.5B to 70B and QwQ-32B; GSM8K, MATH, AIME, KnowLogic. In-distribution ROC-AUC above 0.7 everywhere, over 0.9 on AIME for the 32B model. ECE mostly below 0.1 (Table 1 range 0.01 to 0.14).
limits: Probe does not generalise from logic to math. Needs white-box access and training data.
agent_relevance: A cheap internal correctness signal exists and is calibrated. For a black-box agent loop the analogue is a check or agreement signal, not self-report.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) same paper, early-exit test
finding: Using the probe as a verifier to stop reasoning at a confident intermediate answer cut tokens without losing accuracy. Hidden states also carry look-ahead information on whether a future answer will be right.
numbers: Up to 24% fewer inference tokens with accuracy not reduced (abstract and intro).
quote: These findings confirm that reasoning models do encode a notion of correctness yet fail to exploit it
limits: 24% is the best case, not an average over all models.
agent_relevance: Stop on a signal instead of running a fixed budget; fits G1.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: o1-like models spend huge compute on trivial items and keep re-solving after the first correct answer. Later solutions add little accuracy and little diversity. Overthinking is worst on easy problems.
numbers: On '2+3' o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens than conventional models. The first solution round was correct in more than 92% of cases and used under 60% of tokens (ASDIV example: 287 tokens, 38.7% of the response).
limits: QwQ-32B-Preview and R1 family only; the efficiency metrics are the authors' own.
agent_relevance: Humans stop too early or late by feeling of rightness; these models almost never stop early. An external stop rule is needed.

source: Chen et al. (2025) same paper, mitigation
finding: Self-training on shorter, first-solution-focused data (SimPO variants) reduces overthinking while keeping accuracy.
numbers: QwQ-32B-Preview on MATH500: token output cut 48.6% with accuracy maintained. One variant row: 96.9 accuracy, 741.8 tokens, 41.9% outcome efficiency, 66.5% process efficiency.
limits: Needs training; not applicable to a scaffold-only agent directly.
agent_relevance: Most tokens after the first correct answer are waste; a scaffold should cap rounds once a check passes.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models (DEER)
finding: At reasoning transition points the method forces a trial answer and reads the model's token confidence in it. If confidence passes a threshold, thinking stops. Training-free.
numbers: 11 reasoning LLMs, 10 benchmarks. CoT length cut 19.1% to 80.1% on average, accuracy up 0.3 to 5.0 points. About 75% of samples contain a 'pearl' point where early exit is already correct. One table: vanilla 83.55 vs DEER 84.45; harder set 43.35 vs 51.05.
limits: Code tasks gave only 19.9% length reduction vs 61.5% on math/science. QwQ-32B only 19.1%. Threshold is empirical.
agent_relevance: Closest published match to feeling-of-rightness stopping inside a loop. Trial answer plus confidence read is a code-checkable stop signal.

source: Wu et al. (2025) Thought Calibration: Efficient and Confident Test-Time Scaling
finding: Stopping is treated as a statistical test. Lightweight probes on hidden states predict whether the reasoning tree is still growing; a calibrated rule gives a guarantee on staying near full performance.
numbers: Three reasoning models, four datasets. Up to 60% fewer thinking tokens in-distribution, up to 20% out-of-distribution, performance preserved. The Consistent probe meets the theory; the Supervised probe stays over-confident.
limits: Out-of-distribution saving is only 20%. Needs probe training.
agent_relevance: Turns a stop rule into a guarantee; novelty plateau is the signal.

source: Fu et al. (2025) Deep Think with Confidence (DeepConf)
finding: Model-internal token confidence filters low-quality reasoning traces during or after generation, replacing equal-weight majority voting. Online mode stops weak traces early.
numbers: AIME 2025, GPT-OSS-120B: 99.9% accuracy at 512 traces vs 97.0% reported baseline; up to 84.7% fewer generated tokens. Models: Qwen3-8B/32B, DeepSeek-8B, GPT-OSS-20B/120B.
limits: Needs token logprobs. Confident wrong traces remain; confidence is not independent of model errors.
agent_relevance: A per-trace rightness signal used to allocate compute. Use as a hint inside code selection, not proof (G4/G5).

source: Yoon et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Better Express Their Confidence
finding: Verbalised confidence of reasoning models is better calibrated than that of non-reasoning twins. The gain comes from slow-thinking behaviours (exploring alternatives, backtracking). Calibration improves as the chain unfolds.
numbers: Six reasoning models, six datasets: strictly better calibration in 33 of 36 settings. GLM-Z1 has 0.07 lower accuracy than GLM-4 on NonambigQA yet 0.037 lower ECE and 0.078 higher AUROC. Non-reasoning models also improve when guided to slow-think by in-context examples.
limits: 3 of 36 settings were not better. Removing slow-thinking behaviours drops calibration.
agent_relevance: Re-checking inside the chain lifts confidence quality. Read confidence late, after work, not at the first guess.

source: Taubenfeld et al. (2025) Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs (CISC)
finding: Weighting each sampled path by the model's own confidence in it lets majority vote reach the same accuracy with fewer samples. Also introduces within-question confidence evaluation because standard metrics predict success poorly.
numbers: Nine models, four datasets: required reasoning paths cut by over 40% on average. Gemma2-9B on MATH: 73% cost reduction at matched accuracy.
limits: Gain depends on the confidence method; scores differ across models.
agent_relevance: Rightness weights help when ranking within one question, which is what a code selector does.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Large models are well calibrated on multiple choice when formatted right. P(True) on their own samples and trained P(IK) both predict correctness. P(IK) rises with relevant context or hints.
numbers: Self-evaluation improves when the model sees many of its own samples. P(IK) generalises partly across tasks but is poorly calibrated on new tasks.
limits: Pre-RLHF Anthropic models; later tuned models are less calibrated on logits.
agent_relevance: Original machine feeling-of-knowing result; baseline for later work.

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?
finding: Verbalised confidence from LLMs is overconfident and clustered at high values. Human-inspired prompts and multi-sample consistency help, but no method wins everywhere. Hard professional-knowledge tasks defeat all.
numbers: Verbalised confidence mostly 80 to 100%. White-box beats black-box only narrowly: AUROC 0.522 to 0.605. Five LLMs including GPT-4 and LLaMA 2 Chat, five dataset types.
limits: 2023-era models; reasoning models do better (c08).
agent_relevance: Do not use one-shot self-reported confidence as the doubt trigger. Use consistency or checks.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without oracle labels, intrinsic self-correction does not help and often hurts. The model cannot judge its own reasoning correctness. Earlier reported gains came from oracle stopping.
numbers: GSM8K standard vs oracle self-correct: GPT-3.5 75.9 to 84.3; GPT-4 95.5 to 97.5. Without oracle, performance falls. GPT-3.5 keeps its first GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time; changes go correct-to-wrong more often than wrong-to-correct.
quote: The fundamental issue is that LLMs cannot properly judge the correctness of their reasoning
limits: Small test sets (100 for HotpotQA), 2023 models, two rounds only.
agent_relevance: Direct support for G1 and G2: an 'are you sure' rethink is harmful; a real signal is the missing ingredient.

source: Hagendorff, Fabi, Kosinski (2023) Thinking Fast and Slow in Large Language Models
finding: On CRT and semantic-illusion tasks, early GPT-3 gives intuitive wrong answers like humans. ChatGPT and GPT-4 avoid the trap, mostly by writing chain of thought. Forcing chain of thought on old models cuts intuitive answers; blocking it on new ones brings errors back.
numbers: 150 CRT tasks. Humans 38% correct (original study 41%, n=3,428). Correct: GPT-3-davinci-003 5%, ChatGPT-3.5 59%, GPT-4 96%. Intuitive answers: davinci-003 80%, humans 55%, ChatGPT-3.5 15%, GPT-4 0%. 'Let's use algebra' on davinci-003: correct 5% to 28%, intuitive 80% to 29%.
limits: Tasks partly generated by the authors; newer models may have seen CRT items. Measures final answers, not rightness ratings.
agent_relevance: Lure-then-override pattern of dual-process theory; chain of thought acts as the override.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking
finding: On controllable puzzles reasoning models show three regimes: simple (plain model beats reasoning model), medium (thinking helps), hard (collapse to near zero). Near collapse the models cut thinking tokens although budget remains. On easy items they find the answer early and then wander.
numbers: Thinking effort rises with complexity up to a threshold near the collapse point, then falls. Tower of Hanoi: N=1-4 accuracy declines with more thinking; N=5-7 slight improvement. Models include o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet thinking.
limits: Later critiques question output-length limits and puzzle design; collapse is not proof of no reasoning.
agent_relevance: Agent needs a difficulty-sensitive stop and a give-up-and-change-approach rule; model self-allocation fails at high difficulty.

source: Sui et al. (2025) Meta-Reasoner: Dynamic Guidance for Optimized Inference-time Reasoning
finding: A contextual multi-armed bandit reads a short progress report each round and picks a strategy: continue, backtrack, switch method, restart. This is the Ackerman and Thompson monitor-and-control loop built around a language model.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini + Meta-Reasoner scores 60.32 / 73.64 / 80.23 on a SciBench table vs CoT 33.12 / 55.71 / 58.10 and SC-CoT 37.33 / 56.67 / 63.81. Game of 24 and TheoremQA also used.
limits: Column meanings not verified from the text extract. Bandit trained on the authors' tasks.
agent_relevance: Template for a code-owned controller with model-written progress reports; matches the program-decides, model-fills-slot design.

source: Tsui (2026) Self-Correction Bench: the Self-Correction Blind Spot
finding: The same injected error is fixed when attributed to the user and missed when attributed to the model. Appending 'Wait' removes most of the gap. Cause traced to training data lacking error-correction sequences.
numbers: 14 open-source non-reasoning models: 64.5% blind spot. 5,306 correction traces of fine-tuning cut it 76.0%. Appending 'Wait' cuts it 89.3%.
limits: Main number is for non-reasoning models; reasoning models show a smaller gap.
agent_relevance: Models do not doubt their own text but do doubt others' text. Supports G5 (judge sees no authorship); a 'Wait' prompt must still be signal-gated per G1.

source: Steyvers et al. (2025) What Large Language Models Know and What People Think They Know
finding: Humans reading LLM answers with default explanations overestimate accuracy. Longer explanations raise user confidence even when they add nothing. Matching the explanation's uncertainty wording to model confidence shrinks the gap.
numbers: Human confidence ECE is much higher than model ECE for multiple-choice and short-answer. Samples: 350 questions (GPT-3.5 55%, PaLM2 50% accuracy); 336-question subset with 63% accuracy and AUC 0.78.
limits: Online participants, two LLMs, 2023-era models.
agent_relevance: Fluent long text creates a false feeling of rightness in readers; supports length-normalised scoring (G5).

source: Kang, Zhao, Song (2025) Scalable Best-of-N Selection via Self-Certainty
finding: Self-certainty (how far the token distribution is from uniform) selects among N samples without a reward model, scales with N and works on open-ended tasks where self-consistency cannot.
numbers: Abstract-level claims only; accuracy deltas not extracted.
limits: Numbers not recorded; check tables before citing.
agent_relevance: A graded rightness score from logits for ranking in code.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) AdaptThink: Reasoning Models Can Learn When to Think
finding: NoThinking beats thinking on simple tasks. Reinforcement learning teaches the model to pick thinking or no-thinking by difficulty, a learned when-to-think choice.
numbers: Math sets: response length of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B cut 53.0% with accuracy +2.4%; a second model cut 40.1% (abstract and results text).
limits: Needs RL training; difficulty is judged by the model itself.
agent_relevance: First-stage choice of how much to think; in a scaffold, a cheap probe pass before heavy search.

source: Sui et al. (2025) Stop Overthinking: A Survey on Efficient Reasoning for LLMs
finding: Survey groups efficiency methods into model-based, output-based (dynamic reduction of steps) and prompt-based. Frames overthinking as the machine form of failing to stop when sure.
numbers: Taxonomy only; no headline number.
limits: Survey; claims inherit from sources.
agent_relevance: Map of the field for later lookup.

source: Ji-An et al. (2025) Language Models Are Capable of Metacognitive Monitoring and Control of Their Internal Activations
finding: A neurofeedback-style in-context test: models can report and steer some of their own activation directions. Ability grows with in-context examples and with variance explained by the direction, but covers only a low-dimensional subset.
numbers: Abstract-level claims only; effect sizes not extracted.
limits: Few directions are monitorable; says little about reasoning-correctness signals.
agent_relevance: Self-report reaches only a slice of internal state; use external checks.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: Mathematical Problem Solving
finding: GPT-4 names skills for math questions and clusters them; giving skill-matched exemplars at test time raises accuracy on GSM8K and MATH. Metacognitive knowledge, not monitoring.
numbers: Improvement on GSM8K and MATH for several strong models; exact gains not extracted.
limits: Effect sizes not recorded.
agent_relevance: Skill label then matched exemplar is retrieval by strategy, relevant to operator choice rather than stopping.

source: Ackerman and Thompson (2017) Meta-Reasoning: Monitoring and Control of Thinking and Reasoning (Trends in Cognitive Sciences)
finding: Framework: an initial feeling of rightness after the intuitive answer decides whether analytic thinking starts; intermediate confidence and feeling of progress decide continue or stop; final confidence decides whether to submit. Origin of the loop used by c05, c06, c15. Not opened this session.
numbers: None recorded this session.
limits: Not opened; from background knowledge, verify in the human-side evidence files.
agent_relevance: Three checkpoints for an agent: after first answer, during work, before submit.

source: Thompson, Prowse Turner, Pennycook (2011) Intuition, reason, and metacognition (Cognitive Psychology)
finding: Low feeling of rightness after the first answer predicts longer rethinking and more answer change. Not opened this session.
numbers: None recorded this session.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Machine analogue is c05: low confidence in a trial answer triggers continued reasoning.

source: Cross-study synthesis: machine rightness signals compared
finding: Internal confidence signals (probes c01, trial-answer confidence c05, token confidence c07, path weights c09) work for stopping and weighting. Self-reported confidence and 'are you sure' rethinking do not (c11, c12). Reasoning models report better calibrated confidence than plain models (c08).
numbers: Stop savings: up to 24% (c01), 19.1 to 80.1% (c05), up to 60% in-distribution and 20% out (c06), up to 84.7% (c07), over 40% fewer samples (c09). Different models and benchmarks; not comparable head to head.
limits: No study compares these methods on one benchmark; all are math or science; none on open-ended or ARC-style tasks.
agent_relevance: Build the stop rule from agreement and check results; treat model-stated confidence as weak.
